input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only audit/inspection right binding us (the Company). It already satisfies several preferred parameters: 30 days' prior written notice, exercise during our normal business hours, HDI bears the inspection cost, and scope limited to records related to payment calculations. It deviates because there is no frequency limit (unlimited inspections), no express confidentiality/independent-auditor requirement for the inspecting party, and no restriction on access to our systems or facilities. The redline adds a once-per-twelve-month cap, confines the review to copies of records that may be provided off-site, bars access to our systems, networks and facilities, and confirms confidentiality treatment (leveraging the existing Section 8 obligations), leaving the acceptable notice, business-hours and cost terms intact.

proposal.summary: Limit HDI's inspection right in Section 3.4 to once per 12 months, require confidentiality, off-site review of copies and no access to Company systems
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3.4 gives HDI an unlimited-frequency inspection right over our records, so we have added a once-per-twelve-month cap, confirmed the review is of copies provided off-site with no access to our systems or facilities, and confirmed the inspecting party is bound by confidentiality. Notice, business-hours and HDI-cost terms are unchanged; we can accept a fallback of one inspection per year on 15 days' notice if needed.

ops.oldText: may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours.
ops.newText: may, no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. Any such inspection shall be conducted by HDI's General Manager or an independent auditor, in each case bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those set forth in Section 8, shall be limited to review of copies of the relevant records provided by the Company (which the Company may provide for review off-site), and shall not include any access to the Company's systems, networks or facilities. All information disclosed in connection with any such inspection shall constitute Confidential Information of the Company.
